name: WebinarGeek
summary: European live and automated webinar platform — viewer-tier pricing, engagement tools, CRM integrations and GDPR-friendly hosting. The vendor states you can now generate a full webinar — including polls, quizzes and a registration page — from a plain-text description, with UTM tracking and post-webinar redirects on the registration page (vendor mail, August 2026).
best_for: marketing and sales teams running live and automated webinars in Europe who want a polished, GDPR-friendly platform with viewer-tier pricing
skip_if: you run occasional small webinars (your video-call tool may cover it), or you need the CRM and localization features that sit behind paid add-ons
honest_knock: The friendly €59 headline is the annual rate for 75 viewers, and the real cost lives in add-ons: localisation, the AI assistant, CRM integrations, RTMP and branding profiles are each €20-59 a month on top, and only a Premium subscription can buy them. A serious webinar stack quickly doubles the base plan. In our test on 21 October 2026 a poll went live with an empty option and no warning, after the third answer we had typed was not saved.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-03 on the vendor's own pricing page, read in EUR in a browser on both billing toggles) The plans are now Premium and Enterprise. The Basic plan we read on 14 September (€69 a month or €49 billed annually, 50 viewers) is no longer on the page, in English or in Dutch. Premium is bought per viewer tier, monthly against annual: €99/€59 at 75 viewers, €129/€79 at 125, €199/€119 at 250, €299/€179 at 500 and €399/€239 at 1,000. The page advertises "save up to 40%", and the annual discount is close to 40% on every tier. Premium carries 100 presenters on stage, an 8-hour session limit, one account user, live captions, AI analysis and restreaming. Enterprise is annual-only and quoted from €349 at 500 viewers, €449 at 1,000, €649 at 2,000 and €849 at 5,000, with a 12-hour session limit, three account users, a custom domain, RTMP, workspaces, and localisation and the Salesforce and HubSpot integrations included. The figures render client-side and a plain fetch retrieves almost none of them. Add-ons are priced per month on annual billing, with monthly in brackets: extra user €10 (€15), localisation €20 (€25), AI assistant €20 (€25), branding profiles €59 (€79, an extra workspace and e-mail domain included), HubSpot €49 (€69), Salesforce €49 (€69) and RTMP streaming €29.50 (€49.50), plus a one-off €495 for online onboarding.

schema_offer.description: Premium (75 viewers), billed monthly — €59 is the annual rate; Basic (50 viewers) is no longer sold, and the page prices by region with a currency switch, so the figure depends on where you buy. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-10-03.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 during the 14-day trial, without a card: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We built an unlisted test webinar with three PDF slides and a poll and ran it as a dry run; we did not publish it or invite anyone.
findings: The poll went live with an empty option. The third answer we had typed was not saved, and nothing warned us: the live poll showed an option with only the placeholder 'Fill in an answer'.
A three-page PDF went through 'Processing', 'Converting to images' and 'Putting everything together' and became three slides, in the right order, in about 35 seconds.

Onboarding created three sample webinars on its own (a live one scheduled for the same evening, an automated one and an on-demand one, all marked 'Sample'). The account opened in Dutch, and switching to English took two separate settings: the language menu in the studio and Account > Settings > Language.

New webinar offers Start from scratch, Generate (AI), Copy or Add to series; Present live, Automated or On-demand; and Public, Unlisted or Private access. 'Offer replay' is on by default, and 'Create and customize' does not publish yet. The title field ignored the first title we typed.

Polls sit under Interactions, next to Call to action, Quiz and Information: single or multiple choice, with a default duration of 1:30, and at the start you choose 'End manually' or 'End after a set time'.

The studio did not open until we allowed browser notifications and then camera and microphone. In the dry run it said 'Only team members and invited test viewers can join' and 'Dry runs aren't recorded and don't collect statistics'. Slides changed straight away with the arrow keys, and ending the dry run reset all interactions.
The viewer link of the unpublished webinar returned 'Not yet published: Publish your webinar first before you can use the registration page.', so a test viewer can only watch after you publish.
